taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America. Keep distinct from Croton fruticosus.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST — BUSH / SHRUBBY CROTON: Follow the stem to a persistent WOODY crown, then inspect a mature leaf edge with a lens for very fine SERRULATE teeth, often slightly wavy. Its mostly ovate to ovate-lanceolate pointed leaves are conspicuously green above, and stems bear star-shaped (stellate) hairs. This shrub is MONOECIOUS (male and female flowers on the same plant): a female flower has three once-forked styles, SIX tips, and the mature capsule is smooth. Do not mistake the narrow-leaved annual C. texensis (separate male/female plants, WARTY female fruit), the woolly annual C. lindheimeri, or the small toothed annual C. glandulosus for a woody shrub. Current owner's two public-ready photos show foliage and flowering branches, NOT the soil-level woody crown or the minutely toothed margin sharply enough for decisive arrows.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis is voucher-backed by the UT Plant Resources Center. Comal is locked by preserved ILLS specimen ILLS00139680 near Canyon Lake. Kerr is locked by Heller's 1894 southern-Texas exploration documenting C. fruticulosus on both banks of the Guadalupe at Kerrville.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Use exact county voucher or field documentation; do not infer local counties from broad Edwards Plateau or southwestern Texas range statements.

best_field_traits: petioles short relative to the leaf blade
bisexual racemes typically several centimeters long
three styles bifid to six terminal segments
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Croton lindheimeri is an annual herb with mostly entire leaves. Croton texensis is annual and strictly dioecious, with narrower mostly entire leaves and unisexual inflorescences.

comparisons.key_distinctions: True persistent WOODY base + finely SERRULATE mature leaf margins. Texas croton is an annual dioecious herb with entire narrow leaves and warty female fruit. Woolly crotons are annual herbs with usually entire margins. C. glandulosus is a serrulate ANNUAL; leaf teeth alone do not establish shrubby croton.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.title: Shrubby croton — woody crown plus minute marginal teeth

steps.what: A woody branch tip alone does not prove a perennial shrub. Photograph the base at ground level; current images do not prove this.

steps.look: Fine sawlike serrulations, often slightly wavy margins
steps.what: Macro image of several mature leaf edges with scale is needed. Do not point arrows at indistinct blur.

steps.look: Male stamens plus female flowers on the same plant
steps.what: C. fruticulosus is monoecious, unlike strictly dioecious C. texensis; document the whole inflorescence.

steps.look: Three bifid styles (six ends), smooth fruit
steps.what: Use photographed female flowers and mature capsules; current two local owner images do not resolve the style ends.

steps.look: C. glandulosus has teeth too, but is a low annual
steps.what: Never identify as shrub croton from serration alone.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: SHRUBBY CROTON = WOODY BASE + TINY LEAF TEETH. Confirm together.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Croton fruticulosus: a genuine woody shrub?
steps: Follow stem DOWN to an enduring WOODY soil-level base.
Lens mature leaf edge: look for tiny serrulations, not just a pointed green blade.
Check mixed male/female flowering structures on the SAME individual.
Photograph a true female flower with SIX terminal style tips and mature smooth capsule.
Rule out the serrulate low annual C. glandulosus and dioecious narrow-leaved C. texensis.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Persistent woody shrub + serrulate edge is the strong field combination; if both cannot be checked, use Croton sp. until reproductive evidence.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Current gallery does NOT visually demonstrate the woody crown or tooth-level margin; licensed Wikimedia female/hair sources are not physically installed yet.

diagnostic_photo_targets.role: Exact female flower and six style tips
